Title: Monorepo scaffold
Description: Initialise pnpm workspace with frontend, backend, db, shared, e2e packages. Add tsconfig.base.json (strict), shared flat ESLint (eslint.config.js) + Prettier, .nvmrc (Node 22 LTS), .env.example, .gitignore, .gitattributes (LF), .editorconfig. Root package.json pins packageManager (pnpm) and cross-platform lint/typecheck/format scripts via pnpm -r. Minimal listen-only backend so 0.2's healthcheck has a port. CI ownership stays in 0.3.
Acceptance Criteria: pnpm install works from root; every package (incl. e2e) extends tsconfig.base; pnpm -r lint and pnpm -r typecheck pass on the empty scaffold; .nvmrc + packageManager pin exact versions; .gitattributes forces LF and scripts run on Windows PowerShell; .env.example exists and grows per ticket.
Test Cases: Locally pnpm install, pnpm -r typecheck, pnpm -r lint all green on the empty scaffold. (CI enforcement of the same commands lands in 0.3.)

Title: Docker compose stack
Description: docker-compose.yml orchestrating postgres (Postgres 18), mailpit, backend, frontend + their Dockerfiles under docker/. docker/postgres/init.sql is the SOLE enabler of btree_gist + citext. Base file is CI/prod-like; auto-loaded docker-compose.override.yml adds bind mounts + polling watchers for Windows hot-reload. Credentials/ports from a root .env seeded from .env.example. Prereq: Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend). (When 4.1 lands, a 5th 'worker' service + its health port join this compose file.)
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up boots all four services on pinned tags; Postgres has btree_gist + citext (from init.sql); Mailpit UI reachable (8025) with SMTP on 1025; the dev override gives backend + frontend hot-reload on file change (polling); each service defines a TCP/port-level healthcheck.
Test Cases: CI smoke test brings up the base file, waits for each service's port healthcheck to pass, and tears down; plus a check that btree_gist is present after up.

Title: CI pipeline skeleton
Description: GitHub Actions on ubuntu-latest, push-to-main + PRs: cached pnpm install -> lint -> typecheck -> unit/integration (Postgres 18 via Testcontainers, no service container) -> coverage. Stages fail fast. Coverage uploaded as a GitHub artifact + job summary; configurable gate with a placeholder threshold (real number set in 7.4). concurrency cancels superseded runs. No e2e stage (added in E7).
Acceptance Criteria: Workflow triggers on push-to-main + PRs; stages run in order and fail fast; integration tests provision Postgres via Testcontainers (no external DB service); coverage report produced, uploaded as artifact + shown in job summary; gate mechanism present and configurable with a placeholder threshold that keeps the empty scaffold green; pnpm store cached across runs.
Test Cases: Pipeline green on the empty scaffold; deliberately breaking a test (or introducing a lint/type error) fails the run and blocks the PR.

Title: DB package + Drizzle + migration tooling
Description: Set up the db package: Drizzle client on node-postgres (pg), drizzle.config.ts, migrate runner (db:generate/db:migrate), seed stub. Schema in db/ as single source with a barrel export. No migrations yet - btree_gist/citext are provided by init.sql (0.2), and the first schema migration is 1.1. Build the Testcontainers helper (template-clone model): boot Postgres 18 once, load the same init.sql, migrate into a template DB, hand each test file a fresh clone.
Acceptance Criteria: db:generate and db:migrate run cleanly against an empty schema; the Testcontainers helper boots Postgres, applies init.sql + all (currently zero) migrations without error, and exposes a fresh cloned DB per test with btree_gist + citext present; pg driver wired; seed stub runs.
Test Cases: The test-db helper boots Postgres via Testcontainers, applies init.sql + all migrations, clones a per-test DB, and asserts btree_gist exists in the clone; db:migrate on an empty schema exits 0.

Title: Users table + migration
Description: Drizzle schema for users: uuid pk (gen_random_uuid()), citext email unique, password_hash (NOT NULL), role pgEnum(user,admin), full_name, created_at/updated_at (timestamptz, UTC). Add citext to init.sql. Partial unique index enforcing a single admin (WHERE role = 'admin'). Create the reusable set_updated_at() trigger function + attach it to users. Data migration inserts the one default admin (admin@physiobook.local, default hash).
Acceptance Criteria: Migration creates users table with case-insensitive unique email, the role enum, and the single-admin partial index; the updated_at trigger fires on update; the default admin row exists after migrate; a second admin insert and a case-differing duplicate email are both rejected.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers): inserting a second admin row is rejected; Alex@x.com vs alex@x.com treated as duplicate (citext); updated_at changes on update; the seeded admin is present exactly once.

Title: Sessions table + migration
Description: Drizzle schema + migration for sessions (id uuid pk, user_id fk -> users, token_hash, expires_at timestamptz, revoked_at timestamptz null, created_at). Backs the stateless-access + server-side session model used by login, refresh, logout, and the per-request revocation check. token_hash stores the hashed opaque refresh-cookie value (see 1.6). Must land before 1.2 (register auto-login creates a session).
Acceptance Criteria: Migration creates the sessions table with an FK to users and a token_hash column; a session can be created, looked up by id, and marked revoked (revoked_at set); expired vs revoked sessions are distinguishable; a session cannot reference a non-existent user (FK enforced).
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers): insert a session, revoke it, query reflects revoked_at; inserting a session for a missing user is rejected.

Title: Registration endpoint
Description: POST /auth/register - validate {email,password,full_name} with the shared Zod schema (z.strictObject; password min 8 / max 72 bytes for bcrypt). Hash with bcrypt (native, cost 12). Insert with role forced to user; map the unique-email violation -> 409 (insert-and-catch). On success create a session, issue a 15-min access JWT (sub, role, session_id), and set the refresh cookie. Return 201 {user, token}. Rate-limited per client address (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT). AS-BUILT: strictObject rejects any unknown field, so a client-supplied role -> 400 (deliberate deviation from the original 'role ignored' AC; see PROJECT_STRUCTURE §6). Add JWT_SECRET + token TTL to config/env.ts and .env.example.
Acceptance Criteria: Valid payload creates a role=user user + session and returns 201 with the user (no password_hash) plus a valid access JWT and refresh cookie; missing fields, password <8 or >72 bytes, or malformed email -> 400; case-insensitive duplicate email -> 409; a client-supplied role (or any unknown field) -> 400 (strictObject); password stored only as a bcrypt hash; register is rate-limited per client address.
Test Cases: inject(): happy path -> 201 with user + token decoding to {sub, role:user, session_id, exp} and the refresh cookie set; validation failures (missing full_name, short/oversized password, bad email) -> 400; case-differing duplicate email -> 409; body with role:admin (or any unknown field) -> 400; stored hash != plaintext and bcrypt.compare succeeds.

Title: Login endpoint
Description: POST /auth/login - verify {email,password} (citext match; bcrypt compare, with a dummy compare on unknown-user to equalize timing). On success create a session, issue a 15-min access JWT carrying sub/role/session_id, and set the refresh cookie. Return 201 {user, token}. Uniform 401 for wrong password and unknown user. Rate-limited per client address (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX / AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS); TRUST_PROXY governs what 'client address' means behind a proxy.
Acceptance Criteria: Correct credentials -> a session row is created, a valid access token (with session_id) is returned, and the refresh cookie is set; wrong password or unknown user -> identical 401; token carries role, exp, session_id; login is rate-limited per client address (429 over the limit).
Test Cases: inject(): valid login creates exactly one session and returns a token decoding to the expected claims incl. session_id; wrong password -> 401; unknown user -> 401 (same body); an expired/negative-TTL token fails verification; excess attempts from one address -> 429.

Title: Auth plugin + role guards
Description: Fastify plugin (via fastify-plugin) that on protected routes: verifies the access JWT (signature + exp) using the shared verify util, loads the session by session_id and rejects if revoked or expired (instant-logout check), then decorates request.user = {id, role, sessionId}. Exposes requireAuth (any valid session) and requireRole(...roles) (explicit role set, no hierarchy). Consistent 401/403 error envelope.
Acceptance Criteria: No/invalid/expired token -> 401; valid token but revoked or expired session -> 401; authenticated user whose role isn't in the route's set -> 403; valid token + allowed role -> handler runs with request.user populated; requireRole('user') rejects an admin (403); requireRole('user','admin') admits both.
Test Cases: inject() on sample guarded routes: missing token -> 401; tampered/expired token -> 401; valid-but-revoked session -> 401 (instant-kill); wrong role -> 403; correct role -> 200 with request.user; admin blocked by a user-only guard -> 403; both admitted by a ('user','admin') guard.

Title: Refresh + logout (session-backed)
Description: POST /auth/refresh - read the httpOnly refresh cookie (an OPAQUE random value, not a JWT), verify it against sessions.token_hash, and if the session is live mint a new access token for the same session_id (no rotation; expires_at is an absolute 7-day horizon). POST /auth/logout (requireAuth, authenticated by the access token) stamps sessions.revoked_at and clears the cookie. Refresh has its own wider rate-limit bucket (REFRESH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX). AS-BUILT: no JWT_REFRESH_SECRET - the cookie is opaque so there is nothing to sign (PROJECT_STRUCTURE §10); REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS exists from 1.3. Wire @fastify/cookie.
Acceptance Criteria: Valid refresh cookie -> new access token (200); missing/expired/revoked session -> 401; logout revokes the session and clears the cookie; after logout, both refresh and any live access token are rejected (via the 1.4 guard); the refresh cookie is an opaque value verified against sessions.token_hash (no signing secret); refresh has its own rate-limit bucket.
Test Cases: inject(): valid cookie -> new access token; no cookie -> 401; after logout, a still-unexpired access token is rejected by a guarded route (instant-kill proof); refresh on a revoked session -> 401.

Title: Frontend auth flow
Description: Login + register forms validated with the shared Zod schemas. AuthProvider/useAuth holding the in-memory access token + user. Typed fetch wrapper: attaches Bearer, and on 401 runs a single-flight /auth/refresh then retries; on refresh failure, clears state -> /login. Silent refresh on app load (rehydrate from the httpOnly cookie) behind an auth-loading gate so guarded routes don't flash to login. Protected routes redirect unauthenticated users to /login (return-to preserved) and redirect wrong-role users to their own area. Role-based nav. Register auto-logs-in into the user area; admin logs in via the same form and lands in the admin area. Logout calls /auth/logout, clears the token, redirects.
Acceptance Criteria: User can register (and is immediately logged in) and log in; admin logs in via the same form and reaches the admin area; the access token is attached to requests, and an expired one triggers a single silent refresh so the original request still succeeds; on reload the session is restored with no flash to login (invalid cookie -> logged out); unauthenticated access to a guarded route redirects to /login with return-to; wrong-role access redirects to the user's own area; nav renders per role; logout returns the app to a logged-out state.
Test Cases: RTL: register/login validation states (shared schemas); the auth-loading gate shows a spinner then content; wrong-role redirect. RTL with a mocked api: concurrent 401s fire /auth/refresh exactly once then retry (single-flight). Playwright E2E: register -> land in user area (auto-login) -> reload stays logged in -> logout -> guarded route redirects to login; plus admin login -> admin area.

Title: GET /auth/me (identity endpoint)
Description: GET /auth/me (requireAuth) - reads the users row named by the validated access token and returns publicUserSchema (the same shape register/login nest under 'user'). Enables the frontend's on-load rehydration (refresh -> me: a credential, then an identity), since /auth/refresh answers {token} alone. Re-reads the row (email/full_name/role are not claims); a missing row -> 401 (account deleted mid-request), not 404. AS-BUILT: shipped in E1.5, not in the original backlog.
Acceptance Criteria: Guarded by requireAuth; returns the caller's public profile read from the DB; unauthenticated -> 401; missing user row -> 401 (not 404).
Test Cases: inject(): valid token -> public profile; no/invalid/expired token -> 401; deleted-user row -> 401.

Title: practice_settings singleton
Description: Table + migration for singleton practice_settings: id (pk, CHECK id=1), timezone (IANA), slot_duration_minutes (kept, seeded 60, not editable - slots stay fixed 1h per domain rule), reminder_lead_hours, cancellation_cutoff_hours, created_at/updated_at (timestamptz + set_updated_at trigger). Seed the default row. GET /settings (any authenticated user) returns the policy fields; PUT /settings (admin only) updates the editable ones. Validate with a shared Zod schema (valid IANA tz; reminder_lead_hours > 0; cancellation_cutoff_hours >= 0). AS-BUILT: PUT validates timezone against Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') plus an explicit allowance for 'UTC' (the one canonical name the ECMA-402 list omits, and the seed default). A client-supplied slot_duration_minutes -> 400 (strictObject rejects it as an unknown field, same deliberate deviation from a literal 'ignored' AC as ticket 1.2 - see BACKEND_DEV.md §2 / PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md §6).
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one settings row (CHECK id=1 + pk) - a second is rejected; defaults seeded to match the domain rules (reminder 24, cutoff 24, slot 60); any authenticated user can read the policy fields; only admin can update (non-admin PUT -> 403); slot_duration_minutes is not editable; invalid timezone or out-of-range values -> 400; the updated_at trigger fires on update.
Test Cases: Integration: a second settings row is rejected. inject(): a user can GET the policy fields; user PUT -> 403; admin PUT valid -> 200 and persists; admin PUT with a bad timezone / negative cutoff -> 400; an attempt to change slot_duration_minutes -> 400 (rejected as an unknown field, not silently ignored; see AS-BUILT note). updated_at changes on update.

Title: Business hours CRUD (admin)
Description: business_hours table (id, day_of_week 0-6 [0=Sun], open/close as TIME wall-clock in the practice tz). Admin edits via PUT /business-hours - whole-week bulk replace: client sends all windows, server validates then swaps them in a transaction. Split shifts allowed (multiple windows/day). Zod validation: day_of_week 0-6, close>open per window, no overlapping windows within a day; open/close may be any time (not restricted to the hour). GET /business-hours readable by any authenticated user. Changing hours does not retroactively affect existing appointments. AS-BUILT: times are HH:MM strings (00:00-23:59, any minute); 24:00 is not accepted, so the latest possible close is 23:59. Windows are half-open, so back-to-back windows (09:00-12:00 + 12:00-15:00) are accepted. An empty week ({ windows: [] }) is valid and closes the practice; the table is not seeded, so no slots exist until the admin sets hours. Request and response share one shape, { windows: [...] } sorted by day then opening time; unknown fields -> 400 (strictObject). Same-day overlap is enforced by the Zod contract; the DB holds the per-row CHECKs (day 0-6, closes_at > opens_at). The replace takes LOCK TABLE ... SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE so concurrent replaces serialize instead of committing the union of two weeks (see SCHEMA.md 2.4).
Acceptance Criteria: Admin bulk-replaces the weekly windows atomically - any validation error rejects the whole replace with no partial write; close<=open, day_of_week out of 0-6, and overlapping same-day windows are all rejected; non-overlapping split shifts are accepted; any authenticated user can read the effective weekly hours; non-admin PUT -> 403.
Test Cases: inject(): valid bulk replace persists all windows; close<=open rejected; day out of range rejected; overlapping same-day windows rejected (replace fails atomically, prior config intact); split shift (09:00-12:00 + 14:00-18:00) accepted; non-admin PUT -> 403; user GET -> 200. Also: back-to-back windows accepted; empty week accepted; unknown fields -> 400. Service (real Postgres): a DB-level failure mid-replace rolls back and keeps the prior week; 8 concurrent replaces leave exactly one submitted week.

Title: Slot generation service + GET /slots
Description: Service computing bookable on-the-hour 1h slots for a practitioner over a practice-tz date range (capped 62 days). A slot [H:00,H+1:00) is bookable iff fully contained in an open business_hours window, not overlapping any active calendar_blocks row (appointment or time-off), and start > now (injectable clock). Computed with Luxon in the practice timezone, converting local wall-clock hours to UTC instants. DST: spring-forward nonexistent hour yields no slot; fall-back repeated hour yields a single slot at the earlier UTC offset. Exposes a shared isSlotBookable(start) helper (reused by 3.2) and a GET /slots endpoint (authenticated; query = date range in practice-tz days, capped 62) returning UTC slot instants for the frontend (2.4 preview, 3.5 picker). Scoped by practitioner_id. (5.3 reuses this grid; factor it to parameterize which blocks to subtract and whether to include past.) DECIDED (settles the 2.2-review open decision): (a) business hours are practice-wide and apply to every practitioner - no migration; business_hours keeps no practitioner_id and the grid is scoped by practitioner_id only on the calendar_blocks side (recorded in SCHEMA.md 2.4 and 8). DECIDED: '62 days' is two rules - the GET /slots query range is capped at 62 practice-tz days (inclusive), and a slot is bookable only inside the booking horizon now < start < now + 62 days, so GET /slots never offers a slot that 3.2's isSlotBookable would reject. The horizon and the past filter are grid parameters, so 5.3 can switch both off. AS-BUILT: GET /slots?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD - practice-tz dates, both inclusive, to >= from, at most 62 days; unknown parameters -> 400 (strictObject); any authenticated role. Response { timezone, slots: [{ start, end }] } with UTC ISO instants, so the frontend can label times without a second call. The pure grid is backend/src/modules/availability/slot-grid.ts: generateSlots({ timezone, windows, from, to, blocks?, within? }) - 5.3 passes time-off blocks only and no within; bookingWindow(now) gives the horizon; isSlotBookable(start, { timezone, windows, now }) is membership of that day's grid inside the booking window and deliberately does not check freeness (3.2 relies on the EXCLUDE). Each window is checked on its own, as the ticket says, so back-to-back windows (09:00-11:30 + 11:30-14:00) yield no 11:00 slot across the seam. Luxon resolves a repeated fall-back hour to its later offset, so the grid steps back to the earlier one explicitly; whole-hour DST shifts are assumed, as in 3.1. Days with a steady UTC offset convert local hours by arithmetic and only DST-switch days use Luxon per hour, and blocks are subtracted in one sorted sweep, keeping a 62-day range in single-digit milliseconds. The practitioner is the single admin row (3.1). New dependencies: luxon, fast-check (dev).
Acceptance Criteria: Returns correct open slots for a range; excludes taken slots and time-off; excludes past slots and slots beyond the 62-day booking horizon; emits on-the-hour slots each fully inside an open window (e.g. 09:30-17:30 -> 10:00..16:00); spring-forward skipped hour absent; fall-back repeated hour yields exactly one slot; over-cap ranges rejected. GET /slots returns bookable slots for a valid range to authenticated users; invalid/over-cap range -> 400.
Test Cases: Fixed-clock unit tests: normal week; containment for a 09:30-17:30 window; fully-booked day -> no slots; time-off excluded; spring-forward day -> skipped hour absent; fall-back day -> single slot for the repeated hour; past slots excluded relative to injected now; slots at or beyond now + 62 days excluded. Property test: generated slots are on-the-hour, mutually non-overlapping, and none overlap active blocks or fall outside business hours. inject(): GET /slots returns expected open slots for a range; over-cap range -> 400. AS-BUILT additions: a UTC-to-local oracle for every hour of 2026 in seven zones (DST at 02:00 and at midnight, southern hemisphere, +05:30/+05:45); a regression for zones whose midnight does not exist (America/Santiago); blocks in any order incl. nested; isSlotBookable rejects the second fall-back occurrence; property: dropping a slot only because a block overlaps it, and isSlotBookable accepts every grid slot. Testcontainers: time-off starting before the range, cancelled/cancelled_by_admin ignored, another practitioner's blocks ignored, timezone read from settings. inject(): exactly 62 days -> 200; reversed range, impossible date, timestamp, missing bound, unknown parameter -> 400; unauthenticated -> 401.

Title: Admin availability UI (+ settings)
Description: Admin availability screen. A weekly-grid editor for business hours (7 days, add/remove windows per day for split shifts, 15-min time inputs); Save issues 2.2's whole-week PUT. Inline validation mirrors the shared Zod rules (close>open, no same-day overlaps, valid day) with a form-level overlap message and a dirty-state guard. Includes a practice-settings section (timezone via IANA picker, reminder_lead_hours, cancellation_cutoff_hours) saved via PUT /settings. A live slot-preview panel calls the 2.3 service to show resulting bookable slots. Admin-only route. AS-BUILT: route /admin/availability (admin-only, nav entry 'Availability'). Server state goes through TanStack Query (new dependency, first server-state screen); saving hours or settings invalidates every cached /slots range, and the query cache is cleared on sign-out. The hours editor lists days Monday first; time inputs step 15 min as a hint only - any minute is accepted, matching the 2.2 contract. Validation runs weeklyBusinessHoursSchema itself, so the editor blocks exactly what the API refuses; a new split-shift window starts at the day's latest close so it does not begin overlapping, and a day that already runs to 23:59 offers no Add (the button is disabled with a visible reason) rather than creating an invalid 23:59-23:59 window.The timezone picker is a free-text field with a datalist of Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') plus UTC (the registry the shared schema checks), so an invalid name can be typed and is rejected inline. The slot preview shows the saved state, not unsaved edits: today plus 6 days counted in the practice timezone, labelled en-GB in that timezone. DEVIATION (agreed when 2.4 was planned): the dirty-state guard is beforeunload only - it guards reload, tab close and leaving the SPA, but NOT in-app navigation (nav links), which still discards unsaved edits silently. React Router's useBlocker needs a data router and the app mounts <BrowserRouter>; migrating to createBrowserRouter was weighed and declined for this story. The Playwright case is deferred to E7 (docs/DEFERRED_TESTS.md); its booking-list half also needs 3.5.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can edit and save both business hours (bulk replace) and practice settings; validation is surfaced inline and overlaps/invalid ranges are blocked before save; after saving, the slot preview reflects the new hours and timezone; non-admin cannot reach the screen.
Test Cases: RTL: add/remove windows; close<=open and same-day overlap show inline errors; dirty-guard on navigate-away (beforeunload only, see DEVIATION); settings form rejects an invalid timezone. Playwright (deferred to E7, see docs/DEFERRED_TESTS.md): edit hours + timezone -> save -> slot preview/booking list updates.

Title: calendar_blocks + appointments + EXCLUDE constraint
Description: Migration creating calendar_blocks (id uuid pk, practitioner_id FK->users(id), kind pgEnum(appointment,time_off), period tstzrange with '[)' bounds in UTC, status pgEnum(active,cancelled,cancelled_by_admin) default active, created_at/updated_at + set_updated_at trigger) with the scoped EXCLUDE USING gist (practitioner_id WITH =, period WITH &&) WHERE status='active'. CHECK (whole-hour-offset assumption documented): for kind='appointment', lower(period) on the UTC hour and upper-lower = 1 hour; time_off exempt (arbitrary range, lower<upper). appointments table (id uuid pk, block_id unique FK->calendar_blocks, user_id FK->users) 1:1 with an appointment block; status lives on the block. Seed uses the admin user as practitioner. (5.1 adds a nullable note column used by time-off.) AS-BUILT: calendar_blocks_period_bounded is stricter than lower<upper - every period (time_off included) must be finite, non-empty and '[)'. The appointment CHECK is calendar_blocks_appointment_on_the_hour and truncates explicitly in UTC, independent of the session TimeZone. practitioner_id has no default and the seed is unchanged: the admin row from migration 0001 is the practitioner, and writers (3.2, 5.1) pass its id. appointments has no practitioner_id, status or timestamps - it reaches all of them through its block. The DB does not check that an appointment's block has kind='appointment'; the only writer (3.2) inserts both rows in one transaction. ON DELETE: appointments.block_id cascades from its block; practitioner_id and user_id are NO ACTION, so a user with ledger history cannot be deleted. See SCHEMA.md 2.5-2.6.
Acceptance Criteria: EXCLUDE present and active - two overlapping active blocks: second rejected at the DB; adjacent blocks ('[)' bounds) do not conflict; cancelled/cancelled_by_admin blocks don't block; appointment blocks must start on the UTC hour and be exactly 1h (off-hour or non-1h rejected); time_off arbitrary ranges allowed; appointment is 1:1 with its block and requires a valid user_id.
Test Cases: Testcontainers: two overlapping active inserts -> second rejected; adjacent [10,11)+[11,12) both accepted (no false conflict); a cancelled block does not block a new overlapping active block; off-hour (10:30) and non-1h (2h) appointments rejected; arbitrary-range time_off accepted; appointment requires unique block_id + valid user_id.

Title: Book appointment endpoint
Description: POST /appointments (requireRole('user')). Payload {start} (UTC ISO); end = start+1h; user_id from the token; practitioner_id = seeded physio. Validate via the shared isSlotBookable(start, { timezone, windows, now }) helper from 2.3 (backend/src/modules/availability/slot-grid.ts): on-the-hour, within business hours, not past, within the 62-day booking horizon (start < now + 62 days, see 2.3) - NO pre-check for freeness. Insert calendar_block + appointment in one transaction; rely on the DB EXCLUDE for freeness, catching the exclusion violation -> clean 409 'slot taken' with full rollback. Return 201 with the created appointment. (4.3 later hooks reminder-job scheduling into this booking flow.) DECIDED: the request body is a strictObject like every other contract, so a payload carrying user_id (or any unknown field) is rejected with 400 and books nothing - the ticket's original 'spoofed user_id still books for the token's user' would have meant silently stripping unknown fields on this one endpoint. AS-BUILT: contract in shared/src/schemas/appointment.ts - request { start } (UTC instant ending in Z; offsets -> 400), response { id, start, end, status } (the appointment id; the same item shape 6.1 lists). Error codes SLOT_TAKEN (409) and SLOT_NOT_BOOKABLE (422) in the closed code list. backend/src/modules/appointments/: the route is requireRole('user') and rate-limited by its own BOOKING_RATE_LIMIT_MAX (default 20, in the AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS window), keyed by the token's user id rather than the client IP - booking runs no bcrypt, so the auth brute-force limit does not fit, and patients behind one NAT must not share a bucket (the guard's onRequest runs before the limiter's, so the user is known); bookAppointment reads timezone + business hours, rejects with 422 unless isSlotBookable, then inserts the calendar_block and the appointment in one db.transaction and inserts the block with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and answers 409 SLOT_TAKEN when it returns no row - any other failure (e.g. an FK error on the appointment insert) propagates and still rolls the block back. AMENDED IN 3.3: originally a plain INSERT mapping 23P01 on calendar_blocks_no_overlap to 409, which deadlocked under concurrent bookings (40P01 -> 500); see 3.3. findPractitionerId moved out of slots.service.ts into backend/src/modules/practitioner/ so slots and booking share it, and the period helpers (periodStart / periodEnd / tstzrangeOf) were extracted into backend/src/lib/period.ts, replacing the copies in the 2.3 slots and 5.1 time-off services. No new dependency or migration; one new env var, BOOKING_RATE_LIMIT_MAX.
Acceptance Criteria: Valid free slot -> 201; taken slot -> 409 'slot taken'; out-of-hours/off-hour/past/beyond-window -> 422; malformed body -> 400; booking is for the authenticated user (user_id from token, not payload); admin (role=admin) -> 403; on conflict the transaction rolls back fully with no orphan block.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: happy path -> 201; taken slot -> 409; out-of-hours / off-hour / past -> 422; conflict rolls back fully (no orphan calendar_block); admin -> 403; a payload naming another user_id -> 400, nothing booked (see DECIDED). AS-BUILT additions: Testcontainers service tests - back-to-back slots accepted; slot under time-off -> 409; cancelled / cancelled_by_admin block does not block; another practitioner's block ignored; 422 for before-opening, ending-after-closing, closed day, already started, beyond the 62-day horizon, fractional second, each writing nothing; hours read in the practice timezone; a failing appointment insert rolls the block back; the appointment insert-returned-no-row guard (the block one became the 409 path in 3.3). inject(): booked slot disappears from GET /slots; slot under time-off -> 409; 400 for empty body, non-string start, date-only, offset timestamp, unknown field; unauthenticated -> 401 before body validation; past the per-user limit -> 429; a second user at the same address still books; the login limit does not apply to booking.

Title: Concurrent booking race test (headline)
Description: The headline concurrency proof. Seed N=20 distinct patients; fire Promise.all of 20 concurrent POST /appointments (.inject()) at one slot against real Postgres (Testcontainers, pool >= N); assert exactly one 201, nineteen clean 409s, zero 500s/deadlocks, and exactly one active appointment/block in the DB. Repeat ~10 iterations. Plus a same-user double-submit variant (one user, N concurrent identical requests) -> exactly one booking. Outcome deterministic regardless of which request wins. AS-BUILT: backend/tests/race/concurrent-booking.test.ts. The 20 patients register through /auth/register (bcrypt at production cost, so that beforeAll has a 60 s timeout); the app is built with databasePoolMax N+5, a new optional buildServer/buildTestApp option (production keeps the pg default of 10). 10 iterations each of the distinct-patient and same-user races, each asserting the exact status counts {201: 1, 409: 19}, SLOT_TAKEN bodies, and a ledger of exactly one active block joined to the winner's appointment. FOUND AND FIXED: the first run deadlocked - two plain INSERTs on an EXCLUDE constraint can each wait on the other's uncommitted conflicting tuple, and the detector's 40P01 surfaced as 500 (2 of 10 iterations, all 19 losers). Booking (3.2) and time off (5.1) now insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: speculative insertion withdraws its own tuple on a conflict instead of waiting, so it cannot deadlock, and 'no row returned' is the conflict. The 23P01 catch and PG_EXCLUSION_VIOLATION are gone. The ON CONFLICT has no target because Drizzle cannot name an exclusion constraint; the only other constraint it could absorb is the uuid primary key. Added backend/tests/race/concurrent-time-off.test.ts: 20 identical time-off POSTs (one 201, the rest 409 naming the winner) and one time-off racing 20 bookings (exactly one active block, never a 500).
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one 201, all others 409 (never 500/deadlock); DB holds exactly one active appointment for the slot with no orphan/partial blocks; the same-user concurrent double-submit yields exactly one booking; stable across repeated iterations.
Test Cases: Testcontainers + Promise.all of N .inject() POSTs (pool >= N): assert status counts (1x201, N-1x409, 0x500) and final DB state; repeat 10x. Same-user variant -> one 201, rest 409, one booking. AS-BUILT additions: time-off vs time-off and time-off vs 20 bookings races (5.1 deadlock fix).

Title: Cancel appointment (24h rule)
Description: DELETE /appointments/:id (requireRole('user')). User cancels their own active appointment only if now <= start - cancellation_cutoff_hours (compared on UTC instants, injectable clock). Flips the block status -> cancelled, freeing the slot (partial EXCLUDE). Returns 200 with the cancelled appointment. Note: when reminders (4.3) land, user-cancel must also cancel the pending reminder job. AS-BUILT: contract in shared/src/schemas/appointment.ts - params { id } (uuid, else 400), response is the same appointmentSchema item as 3.2 with status 'cancelled'; new error code CANCELLATION_CUTOFF_PASSED (422), the 409 reuses ALREADY_CANCELLED from 5.1. The cutoff is inclusive (cancel at exactly start - cutoff succeeds) and read from practice_settings.cancellation_cutoff_hours on every request; with a cutoff of 0 an appointment is cancellable until it starts. cancelAppointment (backend/src/modules/appointments/appointments.service.ts) is one conditional UPDATE of the block (owned by the caller, active, lower(period) >= now + cutoff), the same pattern as 5.1's time-off cancel, so concurrent cancels cannot both succeed; a miss is classified in the order 404 -> 403 -> 409 -> 422, so another user's appointment is 403 whatever its state. A time-off block id is 404 (only appointment ids are looked up). Admin -> 403 (requireRole('user')); admin hard-cancel is E5. No rate limit, no new dependency, migration or env var.
Acceptance Criteria: Cancel at >cutoff -> 200 and the slot becomes re-bookable; within cutoff -> 422; another user's appointment -> 403; non-existent -> 404; already-cancelled -> 409; only active appointments are cancellable.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers (fixed clock): cancel at 25h -> 200, slot re-bookable after; at 23h -> 422; cross-user -> 403; non-existent id -> 404; second cancel of the same appointment -> 409. AS-BUILT additions: inject() - cancelled slot reappears in GET /slots and another user books it; non-uuid id -> 400; unauthenticated -> 401 before param validation; admin -> 403, appointment untouched. Testcontainers service tests - exactly at the cutoff -> cancelled; 1ms inside the cutoff and after the start -> 422, block stays active; cutoff read from settings (48h); cutoff 0 cancellable until start; another user's cancelled appointment -> 403; time-off block id -> 404; cancelled and cancelled_by_admin -> 409; the user's other appointments untouched; two concurrent cancels -> exactly one succeeds, the other 409.

Title: Booking UI (slot picker)
Description: User booking page (requireRole('user') route). Fetches bookable slots from GET /slots (2.3) for the selected date/range, rendered in the practice timezone (tz label) with date navigation; shows only open slots with an empty-state when none. Click a slot -> confirm dialog (date/time in practice tz) -> POST /appointments with optimistic feedback: on 201 confirm + update list; on 409 revert, show 'slot just taken', and refetch. Graceful two-tab race handling.
Acceptance Criteria: User sees only open slots in practice tz; booking updates the list; 409 handled gracefully with a refetch; confirm dialog precedes booking; empty-state when no slots; page is user-only.
Test Cases: RTL: picker rendering + absent taken slots; confirm-dialog flow; 409 revert + message (mocked api). Playwright: book end-to-end; two-tab race (second tab sees 'slot taken').

Title: pg-boss integration + worker
Description: Wire pg-boss on the shared Postgres (pg-boss manages its own schema on start()). Separate jobs/worker.ts process as its own compose service (5th service), exposing a tiny /health HTTP endpoint (reports pg-boss connected) for the compose healthcheck. Shared pg-boss config module (jobs/boss.ts: queue names, createBoss/startBoss): the API enqueues via a send-only JobQueue decorated as app.jobs (delayed jobs use send's startAfter), the worker consumes (work); maintenance/cron run in the worker only. Entrypoint src/worker.ts -> startWorker() in jobs/worker.ts, own env schema (DATABASE_URL, WORKER_HEALTH_PORT; no API secrets); /health runs SELECT 1 through pg-boss and answers 503 when disconnected. Graceful SIGTERM -> boss.stop({graceful, 20s}); compose stop_grace_period 30s. At 4.1 only a no-op handler.
Acceptance Criteria: pg-boss schema created on start; the worker service boots, registers handlers, and its /health reports healthy; a no-op job enqueued by the API is processed by the worker exactly once; the worker shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers, in-process pg-boss): enqueue a no-op job via the API (app.jobs) -> the worker handler processes it exactly once; pg-boss schema absent before start and present after; /health 200 while connected and 503 after pg-boss stops; graceful close waits for an in-flight job (and closes /health even if pg-boss stop fails); a SIGTERM during boot still drains and exits 0. docker-smoke: worker healthy, no-op round-trip through the running container, exit 0 on SIGTERM.

Title: Email transport + Mailpit
Description: mailer.ts over nodemailer SMTP: Mailpit (:1025) in dev/test, real SMTP creds in prod - swappable by env (MAIL_* + MAIL_FROM in config/env.ts + .env.example). Messages built by typed template functions returning {subject, text, html} (minimal inline HTML). Test harness gains a Mailpit Testcontainer helper (send via SMTP :1025, assert via the :8025 HTTP API). AS-BUILT: MAIL_* live in the WORKER env only (MAIL_HOST, MAIL_PORT, MAIL_FROM required with no default; MAIL_SECURE defaults to false; MAIL_USER/MAIL_PASSWORD set as a pair) - mail is sent from jobs, so the API holds no SMTP credentials, and compose moved the unused SMTP_* off the API onto the worker as MAIL_*. Templates are built with defineTemplate() (lib/mail-template.ts): text and html rendered from the same paragraphs, every value HTML-escaped; no production template ships here (4.3/4.4 add theirs). The Mailpit Testcontainer boots once per run in global-setup next to Postgres; tests isolate by a unique recipient (tests/helpers/mailpit.ts). The worker process does not yet construct the mailer - 4.3 wires it in with its first consumer.
Acceptance Criteria: Mail sent in dev/test lands in Mailpit; transport swappable by env; each mail has a templated subject + text/html; missing mail config fails fast at boot.
Test Cases: Integration (Mailpit Testcontainer): send a templated mail -> assert it appears via Mailpit's HTTP API with the expected subject/recipient.

Title: Schedule + send 24h reminders
Description: notification_log(dedupe_key UNIQUE, type, recipient, sent_at) for exactly-once. On booking (hook into 3.2), schedule a pg-boss job at start - reminder_lead_hours; skip if booked inside the window. At fire time the handler: (1) self-guards - skips if the appointment is no longer active; (2) sends the user's individual reminder (claim reminder:user:{apptId}); (3) if the appointment is the earliest active appointment of its contiguous run, sends one grouped admin mail counting the active run with singular/plural wording + a list, claiming reminder:admin-run:{runStartInstant}. Rendered in practice tz. Changing reminder_lead_hours later does not reschedule existing jobs. The worker entrypoint builds the 4.2 mailer (createMailer(mailerConfigFromEnv(env))), hands it to the reminder handler and closes it on shutdown - deferred from 4.2, which had no consumer for it. (7.3 requires an env-guarded clock-advance/due-job trigger, enabled only under the E2E flag.)
Acceptance Criteria: Reminder fires ~lead before; an active appointment -> the user gets an individual mail; the run's earliest active appointment triggers exactly one grouped admin mail counting adjacent active appointments (singular vs 'N appointments starting at HH:MM' + list); a cancelled appointment produces no mail and is excluded from the admin count; no reminder scheduled when booked inside the window; a retried job yields one log row / one mail.
Test Cases: Fake clock, Testcontainers + Mailpit: single appt -> user mail + admin mail (count 1, singular); three consecutive -> one grouped admin mail (count 3, plural, listed) + three user mails; cancel one of the run pre-fire -> admin count excludes it; cancel the run-start -> the next active appt sends the grouped mail; job run twice -> one log row / one mail; booked <lead out -> no reminder; non-consecutive appts -> separate admin mails.

Title: Cancellation notifications
Description: On admin hard-cancel (5.2), enqueue a send-cancellation pg-boss job; the worker sends the affected user a cancellation email via mailer (retry on failure), deduped via notification_log (cancellation:{apptId}). Content: the appointment's date/time (practice tz), cancelled by the clinic. The reminder is already suppressed by 4.3's self-guard (no active job cancellation needed). Only admin hard-cancel triggers this. AMENDED IN 5.2: the enqueue side is done - 5.2 sends the 'send-cancellation' job (payload { appointmentId }, Zod schema in backend/src/jobs/send-cancellation.job.ts) inside the cancel's transaction (pg-boss fromDrizzle), so every admin cancel has exactly one job. The worker's handler is a PLACEHOLDER that validates the payload and completes the job without sending anything: until 4.4 deploys, admin cancels send no email. To keep mail from being lost by accident, 4.4 must replace sendCancellationHandler in place (same queue name and payload - do not add a second queue or change the enqueue), let a send failure throw so pg-boss retries instead of completing the job, and add a test that the worker's default handler for 'send-cancellation' actually sends mail.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin hard-cancel -> the user receives exactly one cancellation email (deduped); the appointment's reminder does not fire (self-guarded); a transient send failure is retried without duplicating.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers + Mailpit): admin cancel -> user cancellation mail in Mailpit; the pending reminder does not fire after cancel; re-running the job -> still one mail.

Title: Book time off (+ remove, overlap error)
Description: POST /time-off (requireRole('admin')) - insert a time_off block over an arbitrary range {start,end} (UTC, start<end, optional note) for the physio. Rely on the DB EXCLUDE; on an exclusion violation, query the overlapping active blocks and return a 409 listing them. DELETE /time-off/:id - flip a time_off block to cancelled, freeing those slots. Active time-off is excluded from bookable slots by 2.3. AS-BUILT: the practitioner is the authenticated admin. Timestamps are UTC ISO with 'Z' only (offsets rejected 400); note is optional, trimmed, 1-500 chars, stored in calendar_blocks.note (migration 0008, CHECK calendar_blocks_note_time_off_only). 201 returns {id,start,end,note}. A range with end <= now -> 422 TIME_OFF_IN_PAST. Overlap -> 409 TIME_OFF_CONFLICT with conflicts[{id,kind,start,end}] (no patient data), read after the EXCLUDE has rejected the insert (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returned no row), so the list can be shorter if a blocker is cancelled in between - never a wrong 409; if the read finds no blocker at all, the insert is retried once, so an empty conflicts[] needs that race twice in a row. DELETE answers 204; it is one conditional UPDATE (kind=time_off, status=active, not yet ended), so concurrent cancels yield exactly one 204. Unknown id, an appointment block or another practitioner's block -> 404; cancelled/cancelled_by_admin -> 409 ALREADY_CANCELLED; already ended -> 422 TIME_OFF_IN_PAST; non-UUID id -> 400. Built on 2.3, so slot visibility is tested end-to-end through GET /slots. AMENDED IN 3.3: the insert was a plain INSERT catching 23P01; the 3.3 race test showed concurrent plain inserts on the EXCLUDE constraint deadlock (40P01 -> 500), so it now uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and a skipped insert feeds the same conflict-read/retry path. Proven by backend/tests/race/concurrent-time-off.test.ts.
Acceptance Criteria: Free range -> 201; a range overlapping an active appointment or existing time-off -> 409 listing the conflicting block(s); booked time-off hidden from bookable slots; DELETE cancels a time-off block and those slots become bookable again; non-admin -> 403; non-existent/already-cancelled handled (404/409). Past range on POST and an ended block on DELETE -> 422.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: free range -> 201; overlap with an appointment -> 409 with the conflict listed; overlap with existing time-off -> 409; slots exclude the time-off afterwards; DELETE frees the slots; non-admin -> 403. Also: concurrent overlapping POSTs -> exactly one 201; concurrent DELETEs -> exactly one 204; range already over -> 422; already-cancelled -> 409; unknown id / appointment block -> 404; 400 validation cases.

Title: Hard-cancel any appointment
Description: POST /admin/appointments/:id/cancel (requireRole('admin')) - cancels any future active appointment regardless of the 24h rule; sets status='cancelled_by_admin', freeing the slot; enqueues the 4.4 send-cancellation job. The 4.3 reminder self-guards (no explicit job cancel). AS-BUILT: response is the shared appointmentSchema item (status 'cancelled_by_admin'), params reuse appointmentParamsSchema (non-uuid -> 400); new error code APPOINTMENT_ALREADY_STARTED (422), the 409 reuses ALREADY_CANCELLED. adminCancelAppointment (backend/src/modules/appointments/appointments.service.ts) is one transaction: a conditional UPDATE of the block (the appointment's, practitioner = the authenticated admin as in 5.1, active, lower(period) > now - no cutoff), then the send-cancellation job is sent on the same transaction via pg-boss send({ db: fromDrizzle(tx, sql) }) (pg-boss's own Drizzle adapter), so a cancel cannot commit without its job nor a job outlive a rolled-back cancel. A miss is classified 404 (unknown id, a time-off id, another practitioner's appointment) -> 409 -> 422; 'already started' means start <= now. DECIDED (4.4 depends on 5.2): 5.2 adds the 'send-cancellation' queue with payload { appointmentId } (Zod, backend/src/jobs/send-cancellation.job.ts) and a placeholder worker handler that only validates the payload - 4.4 replaces the handler and sends the mail; no API change needed. No migration, env var or new dependency.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin cancels any future active appointment at any time -> 200, slot re-bookable, cancellation job enqueued; a past appointment -> 422 (already started); already-cancelled -> 409; non-existent -> 404; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: admin cancels a same-day (future) appt -> 200, slot re-bookable, cancellation job enqueued; non-admin -> 403; past appointment -> 422; already-cancelled -> 409. AS-BUILT additions: inject() - job lands in pgboss.job once, slot back in GET /slots and re-booked, 401 without token, 404 unknown id, 400 non-uuid. Testcontainers service tests - cancel at/after the start -> 422 with no job; cancelled and cancelled_by_admin -> 409 with no job; time-off id and another practitioner's appointment -> 404; failing enqueue -> appointment stays active (atomicity); two concurrent cancels -> exactly one success and one job. tests/jobs/transaction-db.test.ts - a job sent through a Drizzle transaction commits/rolls back with it.

Title: Workload dashboard endpoint
Description: GET /admin/workload?from&to&granularity=day|week (requireRole('admin')). Reuses 2.3's factored slot-grid: capacity = business-hours slots minus time-off (past included, appointments not subtracted); booked = active appointments; open = capacity - booked. Aggregated by practice-tz day or ISO (Mon-start) week; range capped 92 days; past + future allowed. Output [{period, capacity, booked, open}]. AS-BUILT: GET /admin/workload?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&granularity=day|week - practice-tz dates, both inclusive, to >= from, at most 92 days; granularity optional, defaults to day; unknown parameters -> 400 (strictObject). The response is a bare array with one entry per period in the range, closed days included as zeros. period is a practice-tz date: the day itself, or the Monday of the ISO week; edge weeks are clipped to [from, to], so a partial week counts only the days inside the range. The practitioner is the authenticated admin (as in 5.1). DECIDED: booked counts every active appointment starting in the period, including one left outside business hours after they changed (2.2 does not retroactively affect appointments); open is the grid minus time-off minus appointments, so it is never negative - for such an off-grid appointment booked exceeds capacity - open, otherwise open = capacity - booked exactly. Only active blocks count; cancelled/cancelled_by_admin and other practitioners' blocks are ignored. The aggregation is a pure function (backend/src/modules/dashboard/workload.ts) over slot-grid.generateSlots with no within: capacity subtracts time-off only, open subtracts time-off and appointments; appointments are bucketed by their practice-tz start date. The 62/92-day inclusive-days helper is shared between the /slots and /workload contracts.
Acceptance Criteria: Correct capacity/booked/open per period; respects business hours and time-off; only active appointments count as booked; empty day -> all-open; full day -> all-busy; a day fully covered by time-off -> capacity 0; day and ISO-week granularity; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: Integration: seeded data yields expected aggregates; empty day all-open; full day all-busy; time-off reduces capacity; week granularity groups Mon-Sun; non-admin -> 403. AS-BUILT additions: pure unit tests - closed days as zeros, partial time-off removes every slot it touches, off-grid appointment counted as booked without touching open, appointment bucketed by practice-local day, out-of-range appointments ignored (incl. same week before from), fall-back day counts the repeated hour once, clipped edge weeks, Sunday evening stays in its local week. Testcontainers: time-off starting before the range, cancelled blocks ignored, another practitioner ignored, timezone read from settings, past week included. inject(): day default, week grouping, exactly 92 days -> 200; over-cap, reversed range, impossible date, missing bound, unknown granularity, unknown parameter -> 400; unauthenticated -> 401.

Title: List all appointments (admin)
Description: GET /admin/appointments (requireRole('admin')) - lists appointments across all patients with start/end (joined from the block), patient name, and status; date-range + status filters (default: upcoming active); ordered by start.
Acceptance Criteria: Returns all patients' appointments for the range (not just the caller's); includes patient + status; default = upcoming active, filterable to past/cancelled; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: returns appointments across users; default shows upcoming active; filter reveals past/cancelled; correct ordering; non-admin -> 403.

Title: Admin dashboard UI
Description: Admin-only dashboard. Appointments list from GET /admin/appointments (upcoming active default, past/cancelled filter) with per-row hard-cancel (confirm -> 5.2). Workload chart (Recharts) from GET /admin/workload with a day/week toggle. Time-off section: range-picker to book (5.1, surfacing the 409 overlap conflicts) + a list of existing time-off with remove (DELETE). Errors inline; times in practice tz.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin sees all appointments (upcoming default, filterable) and the workload chart; can book time off (overlap error surfaced), remove it, and hard-cancel from the list; non-admin cannot reach the screen.
Test Cases: RTL: appointments list + filter; workload chart render; time-off form validation + overlap error; hard-cancel confirm. Playwright: book time off (incl. overlap error), remove time off, hard-cancel flow.

Title: List user appointments endpoint
Description: GET /appointments/me (requireRole('user')) - returns the caller's own appointments grouped {upcoming, past}: upcoming soonest-first, past most-recent-first, each {id, start, end, status} in UTC (active + cancelled). Each upcoming appointment includes a server-computed canCancel flag + cancellableUntil (from cancellation_cutoff_hours), matching 3.4's enforcement. Past capped/paginated (limit); user_id from the token; excludes other users'.
Acceptance Criteria: Returns only the caller's appointments, grouped upcoming/past with correct ordering; includes status (active + cancelled); each upcoming carries canCancel/cancellableUntil consistent with 3.4; excludes others'; unauthenticated -> 401.
Test Cases: inject(): returns own only (not others'); upcoming soonest-first, past most-recent-first; cancelled appear with status; canCancel true outside cutoff and false within; unauthenticated -> 401.

Title: User panel UI + nearest-appointment countdown
Description: User panel (requireRole('user') route). Lists appointments from GET /appointments/me (grouped upcoming/past, cancelled shown with status), times in practice tz. Live countdown to the soonest upcoming appointment (ticks; rolls to the next when it passes). Per-upcoming cancel gated by the server's canCancel: disabled within the cutoff with an explanation, else DELETE /appointments/:id (3.4) -> refetch; a 422 (lost race) surfaces a message. Empty-state with a link to book.
Acceptance Criteria: Panel shows upcoming + past (cancelled tagged); the countdown ticks to the nearest upcoming and advances when it passes; cancel is disabled within the cutoff with an explanation (driven by canCancel); an eligible cancel succeeds and updates the list; empty-state links to booking.
Test Cases: RTL: countdown with fake timers; disabled-cancel state (canCancel=false) + explanation; eligible cancel flow (mocked api) + refetch; empty-state. Playwright: view panel + cancel an eligible appointment.

Title: E2E: full booking journey (+ CI e2e stage)
Description: Playwright journey: register (auto-login) -> book a slot >24h out -> see it in the panel -> cancel (eligible); plus a logout/login assertion. Builds the CI e2e stage deferred from 0.3: GitHub Actions boots the docker-compose stack, waits for healthchecks, migrates, runs a dedicated e2e seed/fixtures (settings + business hours + admin so bookable slots exist), runs Playwright against the compose frontend, uploads traces on failure, tears down. Fresh DB per CI run (empty volume + reseed).
Acceptance Criteria: The full journey passes against the docker-compose stack; the e2e stage runs in CI on a freshly seeded stack; the dedicated e2e seed produces a known bookable schedule; traces uploaded on failure.
Test Cases: Playwright green in CI against compose: register -> book -> panel -> cancel, plus logout/login.

Title: E2E: two-user slot race
Description: Playwright: two browser contexts (two seeded patients) poised on the same slot; clicks fired together (Promise.all at the confirm step). One books; the other sees a graceful 'slot taken' and the slot disappears (refetch). Asserts both UI outcomes and, via a direct Postgres count, exactly one active appointment. Runs on the 7.1 compose stack/seed.
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one context books; the other gets a clear 'slot taken' message; a direct DB count confirms exactly one active appointment; no partial state.
Test Cases: Two contexts -> one success + one conflict UI; direct DB count = 1 active appointment.

Title: E2E: notification flows via Mailpit
Description: Playwright + compose Mailpit. An env-guarded test-only hook (enabled only under an E2E flag, absent in prod) advances the clock / fires due reminder jobs so reminders trigger without real waiting. Scenarios: single-appointment reminder (user mail); grouped-admin reminder (book consecutive slots -> one counted admin mail); admin hard-cancel -> cancellation email. Asserts via the Mailpit HTTP API (subject, recipient, grouped count/list).
Acceptance Criteria: Individual + grouped-admin reminders (correct count) and the cancellation email appear in Mailpit for the scripted scenarios; the trigger hook is disabled outside E2E.
Test Cases: Playwright drives each flow, advances time via the guarded hook, asserts Mailpit contents (recipients, grouped admin count).

Title: Coverage gate + timezone/DST suite
Description: Flip 0.3's placeholder coverage gate to a real enforced threshold: global 90% lines + branches (excluding migrations/config/generated), blocking merges below it in CI. Add a consolidated Luxon timezone/DST suite spanning booking (3.2), slot generation (2.3), and reminders (4.3): spring-forward and fall-back transitions (Europe/Warsaw, fixed known dates).
Acceptance Criteria: The gate blocks merges below 90% lines + branches; excluded paths (migrations/config/generated) not counted; the DST suite passes for both spring-forward and fall-back across booking, slots, and reminders.
Test Cases: CI fails below threshold (verified via a deliberate uncovered path); DST tests green for both transitions.
